newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni journalist killed in latest poll violence. [CORRECTED 06:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Yemeni journalist killed in latest poll violence. [CORRECTED 06:20 GMT]

text.p: A Yemeni journalist was killed and four other people injured when supporters of two rival candidates in Yemen's general elections exchanged fire outside a polling station, a security official said on Thursday.
The official said the shooting, the latest violence to mar the country's elections, took place late on Wednesday.
"A journalist was killed when supporters of different candidates shot at each other after vote counting in Lahaj (corrects from Kahaj) governorate," he said.
An Arab election observer was among the injured, he added.
The killing raised to at least 21 the number of poll-related deaths but officials have played down the shootings as criminal. Election observers note that many Yemenis carry weapons.

Yemenis voted on Sunday in the first general elections since a 1994 civil war and the country's ruling General People's Congress (GPC) has swept more than 60 percent of constituencies in counting so far.

The Islah Party, the GPC's junior coalition partner lagged far behind with less than 20 percent. Islah on Wednesday accused the Supreme Elections Committee of bias, threatening court action over the results.
Final results were expected later on Thursday.
